intended_object: The standard K-algebra isomorphism between the coordinate ring of the additive group 𝔾_a over a commutative ring K, here Sym_K(K), and the polynomial ring K[T]. It sends the universal coordinate ι(1) to T, as in Milne's description 𝒪(𝔾_a) = k[T]. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemma `additiveGroupCoordinateAlgEquiv_coordinate`.
explanation:
In this library the coordinate ring is `SymmetricAlgebra K K`, the symmetric algebra of the rank-one free module. The definition chains two Mathlib isomorphisms:
- `SymmetricAlgebra.equivMvPolynomial` for the singleton basis {1} of K over itself, which gives Sym_K(K) ≃ MvPolynomial Unit K;
- `MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv`, which gives MvPolynomial Unit K ≃ K[X].

Under the resulting K-algebra isomorphism, ι(1) goes to X; the library proves this in the lemma right after the definition. This is exactly the standard identification 𝒪(𝔾_a) ≅ K[T].

It holds over any commutative ring K, which is the natural generality for the additive group scheme. Mathlib has no single declaration for this particular rank-one identification; it only has the two pieces composed here. So nothing is missing and the setting is not too narrow.
